dossier.summary: The project is a Monte-Carlo study of regression-based GATE estimators. It covers five one-hop outcome mechanisms, five graphs (three synthetic, two Facebook) and Bernoulli versus graph-cluster designs, with 300 draws per configuration. Every table number traces to a delivered result file produced by a recorded run. The best-supported findings are these: correctly specified OLS has small bias, with SD scaling close to n^-1/2 and to sqrt(d) on WS; a misspecified saturating response gives a bias that does not shrink with n and is linear in gamma; and on SBM/WS, cluster randomization removes most of that bias. Several headline statements reach further than this evidence. The 'key quantity' mechanism (distance of exposures from the all-treated point) is never measured and is contradicted by the paper's own p sweep. The plug-in SD 'from the design matrix alone' uses the true noise variance. The n and gamma sweeps use a single misspecified mechanism on one realisation per graph family. Several ranges quoted in the text disagree with the paper's own appendix table, though none changes a main conclusion: Hajek and GBM ratios, coverage of 0.93–0.97, the Stanford3 median ratio of 3.2, and BA described as having 'many' clusters when it has 10. Uncertainty is computed (bootstrap RMSE intervals, Monte-Carlo SEs) but shown only in Figure 1, not in the tables. The limitations section is candid about the synthetic, one-hop scope.

claims.quote: When the regression is correctly specified, error is almost pure variance, scales like $n^{-1/2}$ and (in Bernoulli designs) like $\sqrt{d}$ in the degree $d$, and can be predicted from the realised design matrix alone
Under misspecification the error is dominated by an extrapolation bias that does \emph{not} shrink with $n$ and grows linearly with interference strength
the key quantity is how far the observed treated-neighbour fraction lies from the all-treated point
cluster randomization with good clusters reduces both bias and variance by an order of magnitude, and the benefit degrades continuously as clusters leak edges
Bernoulli designs observe neighbour exposures concentrated near $p$, so they extrapolate the most
Naive heteroskedasticity-robust intervals attain nominal coverage only when heterogeneity covariates are included, otherwise coverage can fall to 17--43\% on real graphs
With very few clusters, or at extreme $p$, all estimators degrade, and a plug-in variance formula based on independent noise underestimates the error

regression-based GATE estimation is accurate (RMSE $\approx0.04$--0.15 on a GATE of 2), and its error is governed by a design-leverage term $c^\top(X^\top X)^{-1}c$ that we can compute \emph{before} running the experiment
gradient boosting helps only when the true response saturates
a Hajek exposure estimator is undefined on most Bernoulli draws

issues.quote: the key quantity is how far the observed treated-neighbour fraction lies from the all-treated point
issues.why: The distance of the observed exposures from the all-treated point is never measured (sim.py stores mean_x_sd=None), and the paper's own E4 sweep runs against it: the sigmoid bias is 1.21 at p=0.5 but only -0.15 at p=0.25 and p=0.75, where exposures lie farther from x=1. The E4 text itself puts the bias down to curvature, not distance.

issues.quote: can be predicted from the realised design matrix alone
issues.why: The plug-in SD in predsd.py multiplies the leverage term by the known true noise variance (1.0, or 1.25 for OLS-frac, times sigma^2), so the design matrix alone is not enough. The 128-configuration summary also pools misspecified and few-cluster settings, where the ratio reaches 5.4 (OLS-rich) and 19 (OLS-frac).

issues.quote: Under misspecification the error is dominated by an extrapolation bias that does \emph{not} shrink with $n$ and grows linearly with interference strength
issues.why: The n sweep (E6) and the gamma sweep (E2) use only the sigmoid mechanism, on one WS graph and one SBM graph. Under cluster designs the misspecified sigmoid error is not bias-dominated (bias <=0.012). Limitation (3) concedes only that the 1.2gamma figure is specific to sigmoid.

issues.quote: cluster randomization with good clusters reduces both bias and variance by an order of magnitude
issues.why: For correctly specified models the SD falls only about 3x (OLS-rich 0.130 to 0.042 on SBM linfrac). The 'good clusters' evidence comes from SBM with oracle planted blocks and from WS, one realisation each. On BA, Stanford3 and (for OLS-frac) ego-FB the cluster design is not better.

Louvain on the BA graph gives only 10 clusters (E1.json nclust=10; WS gives 35). That is as few as Stanford3, whose failure the paper attributes to the small number of clusters. The BA cluster-design failure is instead described as unexplained and put down to hubs.

issues.quote: gradient boosting helps only when the true response saturates
issues.why: The paper's own Appendix B table shows GBM with the lowest RMSE on BA quad cluster (0.32 vs 0.38 for OLS-rich) and beating OLS-rich on Stanford3 linfrac cluster (0.15 vs 0.28). Neither response saturates.

issues.quote: For correctly specified models (\texttt{linfrac}, \texttt{inter}) OLS-rich and Poly with HC1 intervals cover at 0.93--0.97 on all graphs and designs
issues.why: E1.json gives Poly coverage 0.917 on BA linfrac cluster, below the stated range. So including the heterogeneity covariate does not always give nominal coverage. Coverage values carry no Monte-Carlo interval (about ±0.013 at 300 draws).

issues.quote: configurations with few clusters (Stanford3: median ratio 3.2, up to 5.4
issues.why: In predsd.csv, 3.2 is the median over only the two Stanford3 linfrac configurations, one of which is a Bernoulli design. Over the five Stanford3 cluster configurations the OLS-rich median ratio is 2.50.

issues.quote: well defined but noisy on ego-FB (RMSE 0.4--1.1, many weights near $p^{d+1}$). With clusters it is comparable to DM on SBM/WS (0.09--0.17) and about 2--3$\times$ worse than a correct regression
issues.why: These baseline ranges disagree with the paper's own Appendix B table and E1.json. Hajek RMSE on ego-FB Bernoulli is 0.63-1.10, cluster SBM/WS is 0.09-0.15, and the ratio to OLS-rich is 2.2-4.4. The GBM ratio stated as 2.5-5x is 2.5-6.2x, and 'Poly up to 2.2' (line 56) omits the 2.47 on BA sigmoid.

issues.quote: Full table (all mechanisms, estimators, intervals) in Appendix~B
issues.why: Table 1 and the Appendix B table give RMSE point estimates only; the bootstrap intervals and Monte-Carlo SEs are in the JSON files but not in any table. Each configuration also uses a single graph realisation (conceded in limitation 2).

issues.quote: We hypothesise (not tested) that, because $x_i$ and $x_j$ share treated neighbours while the omitted component is fixed, the independence assumption in the sandwich fails exactly when the omitted heterogeneity varies with graph position
issues.why: OLS-frac and OLS-rich differ in c, zx and the log-degree term, so the coverage gap is not tied to the heterogeneity covariate alone. The paper concedes the explanation is untested.

issues.quote: Hence the estimator is accurate but its \emph{sample size is effectively $n/d$}
issues.why: The sqrt(d) scaling is measured only on Watts-Strogatz graphs with Bernoulli design (E3). The n/d effective-sample-size reading is extrapolated from that heuristic to the general claim.

issues.quote: for linear-type mechanisms GBM has RMSE 0.26--0.8 under Bernoulli, 2.5--5$\times$ worse than OLS-rich, and only $60$ repetitions were run
issues.why: GBM runs with fixed default-like settings (150 iterations, learning rate 0.1), no tuning and 60 draws against 300 for OLS. No standard Horvitz-Thompson or fractional-exposure estimator is included. The paper concedes the GBM settings (limitation 8).

presentation.why: Figure 1 packs 8 panels at full text width with tick labels and titles of about 5pt; the legend appears only in the first panel and several lines overlap.
Figure 2's three panels have very small axis labels and legends; the right panel's graph-family legend is barely readable at print size.
No figure shows the simulation pipeline or the exposure/extrapolation idea, which carries the main argument.
The Appendix B table has no caption or number (the text calls it 'Table B') and floats onto the checklist page.

Phrases such as 'worse than the truth by a bias of about 1.2gamma', 'Smallest RMSE across rows is only meaningful within a row' and the self-reference '(Sec. 4, E4)' for the cluster-count argument are hard to follow.
Appendix A lists script names (run_all.py, analyze.py, maketab2.py, predsd.py) and truncated file hashes; limitation (10) describes a debugging pass that was overwritten.
The checklist states 'about 15 minutes of wall-clock on a 40-core CPU', while Appendix A says roughly 12 minutes on 36 processes.

paper_mismatches.why: Louvain on the BA graph returns 10 communities (E1.json nclust=10), not many; WS returns 35.

paper_mismatches.paper_quote: $\dagger$: estimator undefined in more than 5\% of draws
paper_mismatches.why: A configuration is reported whenever at least 3 draws are valid. SBM lincount/inter Bernoulli Hajek RMSE (2.91, 1.52) rests on 3 of 300 draws, and only a dagger flags this.

problems.why: Data, cache, results and figure paths are hard-coded to /work (lib.py line 2, sim.py line 3, analyze.py line 4), so the code runs only in that directory layout.
The ego-Facebook edge list was left out of the delivery; it must be downloaded again (URL and hash are in the README).
Regenerated tables must be pasted into main.tex by hand (README), and text numbers were typed by hand from analysis.txt and predsd.csv.
main() uses a fixed Pool of 36 processes, and BLAS threads must be limited by hand to avoid oversubscription.

process_notes: The first full run hung from BLAS thread oversubscription and was killed; a relaunch with single-threaded BLAS completed with R=100.
R was then raised to 300 (GBM 60) and linfrac was added to E3; this final run produced every reported JSON before the paper text was written.
Text numbers were revised in one scripted pass on main.tex (steps 28-30) to match the analysis outputs. No experiment was rerun after the paper first used results.
Total recorded span is about 44 minutes.

integrity.why: This is a simulation study with no tuning. After inspecting the R=100 results, the only changes were raising R to 300 (GBM 60) and adding linfrac to the E3 grid. No estimator, configuration or result was picked by its score, and all configurations are reported.

The metric and estimator code in sim.py was not changed after the first results. The change from R=100 to R=300 is disclosed in limitation (10). Adding linfrac to E3 widens the grid and does not favour any result.

The true GATE is used only to compute errors and coverage. The estimators use the observed Y, the design and the graph (Hajek uses the known design probabilities) and never the truth or the noise-free outcomes.

The tables were generated by scripts from the final JSONs. Text numbers were typed into main.tex by hand from printed run outputs (analysis.txt, the predsd summaries and the Hajek NaN check). A few typed ranges do not match those outputs ('0.4–1.1', '0.09–0.17', 'Poly up to 2.2', '2–3x'), but they look like transcription errors in ranges, not values with no run behind them.
